speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Anterior Hip Dislocation (Posterior force on extended, adducted hip; presentation with leg shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated is classic for anterior dislocation).

I have already requested the necessary imaging to confirm the diagnosis and assess for associated fractures. Please await the X-Ray results.
